instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file, with the updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures (i.e., a principal spending report).

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B) (2025) (updated registration due last day of January, May, and September) and § 101.73(D)
instantiated_cells.justification: Employers must file expenditure statements with updated registrations due three times per year (Jan/May/Sep), making the cadence triannual.
The statute specifies filing with updated registrations due by the last day of January, May, and September, not once per year.
Updated registration (with expenditure statement) is due three times per year rather than every quarter.
The filing cadence is Jan/May/Sep (three times yearly), not twice yearly.
Nothing in the statute requires monthly expenditure statements; it ties filing to the triannual updated registration.
The only cadence specified for employer expenditure statements is filing with the Jan/May/Sep updated registration statements.
An employer's expenditure statement must show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.
The statute expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents engaged by an employer' from the employer's reportable expenditures.
The employer statement's 'expenditures' definition excludes 'the expenses of maintaining office facilities,' which are typical indirect costs.

Reportable 'expenditures' include gifts and items of value such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and such expenditures to specific covered officials must be described in the statement.

When expenditures are made to benefit a particular covered official, the filer must provide item-level identifying details (recipient name, amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client).
For reportable expenditures to specific covered officials, the statement must include 'the specific items of legislation, if any' for which the expenditures were made.
Section 101.73(C) governs the employer's expenditure statement and requires totals but does not require listing legislative agent names.

While an employer's updated registration statement may cover multiple engaged legislative agents, the employer expenditure statement provisions do not require listing those lobbyists on the spending report itself.

The employer expenditure-statement section specifies totals and (where applicable) recipient/legislation details, but contains no requirement to disclose lobbyist addresses or other contact information.
The employer expenditure statement requirements do not include the employer's name/address (those appear in the registration statement under § 101.72(A)(2), not the spending report requirements).
Section 101.73 sets out expenditure reporting elements and does not require the employer to describe its business nature.
The employer spending report is limited to expenditures and does not require reporting lobbying contacts.
The statute calls for 'specific items of legislation, if any,' not general issue areas, indicating general issues are not required in the expenditure statement.
No provision in the employer expenditure-statement requirements mandates disclosure of the employer's major financial contributors.

Registration statements must include agent/employer information and descriptions of legislation (and later specific bills/resolutions), but the statute does not require including names of bill members or sponsors.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because no 'other' cadence applies beyond the specified Jan/May/Sep schedule, there is no other cadence to specify.
